subject: Civil Engineering
title: The I-35W Bridge Collapse
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The I-35W Bridge Collapse.

hook.text: On August 1, 2007, an eight-lane bridge fell into the Mississippi during rush hour.

buildup.text: The I-35W bridge in Minneapolis was a steel truss built in 1967 — forty years old.

discovery.text: Investigators found gusset plates — the steel connectors — were half as thick as needed.

twist.text: Construction equipment for a repaving project added extra weight the day it fell.

climax.text: After the collapse, Congress funded inspection of every structurally deficient bridge.

punchline.text: Undersized connectors hid in plain sight for forty years.

quiz.question: What was the root cause of the I-35W bridge collapse?
options: Gusset plates were undersized in the original design
A ship struck one of the bridge piers

details.summary: The Interstate 35W bridge over the Mississippi River in Minneapolis collapsed on August 1, 2007, killing 13 people. The steel deck truss bridge failed when undersized gusset plates at a critical node could no longer support the bridge load plus construction equipment weight.
details.whyItMatters: The I-35W collapse revealed that connection design errors can remain hidden for decades and highlighted the urgent need for improved bridge inspection and load rating procedures across the United States.
takeaways: Gusset plates at a critical node were half the thickness needed for the design loads
Construction equipment on the bridge added load that triggered the weakened plates
The original 1967 design error went undetected through 40 years of inspections

faq.question: Why were the undersized gusset plates not detected during 40 years of bridge inspections?
faq.answer: Bridge inspections typically assess visual deterioration like corrosion, cracking, and section loss. Load-rating analysis verifies that existing members can carry current traffic loads.

faq.question: What changes resulted from the I-35W bridge collapse?
faq.answer: The Federal Highway Administration mandated gusset plate load ratings for all steel truss bridges nationwide. Peer review requirements for bridge design were strengthened. Construction loading analysis on existing bridges became mandatory before placing heavy equipment.
